title: School teacher recruitment
kicker: CTET / State TET, KVS–NVS and state teacher exams

value.body: Becoming a school teacher in India usually takes three things: a professional teaching qualification (D.El.Ed for primary, B.Ed for upper-primary and secondary), passing a Teacher Eligibility Test (the central CTET or a State TET), and then clearing a recruitment exam run by a state, or by CBSE for Kendriya Vidyalayas (KVS) and Navodaya Vidyalayas (NVS). Private schools set their own hiring rules but often ask for the same qualifications.

items.label: CTET qualifying mark
items.note: 90 of 150; states may allow relaxation (e.g. 55%) for reserved categories

items.note: NCTE extended TET validity from 7 years to life in 2021

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Paper 1 of CTET / TET is for Classes 1–5 and needs Class 12 plus D.El.Ed (or equivalent); Paper 2 is for Classes 6–8 and needs a graduate degree plus B.Ed (or D.El.Ed). A 2023 Supreme Court ruling (Devesh Sharma v. Union of India) held that B.Ed alone does not qualify for primary (Classes 1–5) posts. PGT posts for Classes 11–12 need a relevant master's degree plus B.Ed. After the TET, you apply to KVS / NVS, state teacher recruitment exams, or school boards' notifications.

value.title: At a glance
items: Passing CTET / TET is an eligibility condition only — it does not by itself give a job.
Each state runs its own TET and recruitment; schedules and vacancy counts vary widely, and some states go years between drives.
B.Ed is a two-year course after graduation; NCTE also runs a four-year Integrated Teacher Education Programme (ITEP) after Class 12.
KVS / NVS posts are central government jobs with all-India transfer liability.

value.title: CTET December 2024: appeared vs qualified
value.note: Pass rates 24.17% (Paper 1) and 12.31% (Paper 2). One session only; results vary between sessions. Qualifying CTET is an eligibility step, not a job offer.
value.source: CBSE CTET result (as reported by Careers360)
